deities: Kalki (tenth and final avatar of Vishnu)
Lakshmi (consort of Narayan, main deity alongside Kalki)

history.period: Built by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II, 18th century (circa 1739-1740s; one travel source estimates about 285 years old - approximate, verify)
history.summary: This is the Kalki Mandir of the Jaipur Walled City - a Hindu temple dedicated to Kalki, the prophesied tenth and final incarnation of Lord Vishnu, with Goddess Lakshmi as the co-main deity. It was built by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II in the 18th century and stands in Sireh Deori Bazar (Tulsi Marg, Badi Chaupar area), opposite the palace gate; the sanctum idols are of Kalki and Lakshmi, and the courtyard has a white-marble horse (Kalki's prophesied mount) carved from a single stone, with a crack on its left leg that devotees regard as a wound. It is widely described as the only (or one of the very few) temples in the world dedicated to Kalki - treat 'only' as a sourced claim, not an established fact. LOCATION NOTE: public sources give the address as Sireh Deori Bazar / Tulsi Marg, Badi Chaupar in the walled city, not 'Sri Ram Path / Sambharia'; the brief's Sri Ram Path/Sambharia descriptor is unsupported by sources and is not used here. CSV town and state (Jaipur, Rajasthan) are correct. Not to be confused with the Oachira Parabrahma temple in Kerala (sometimes linked to Kalki) or other Kalki sites. One travel site repeats a legend that it was built in memory of Jai Singh's grandson Kalki Singh; this is a folk account, not documented history. Coordinates from Wikipedia (26.9262837, 75.8268671).

name: Kalki Temple
town_description: Jaipur, the capital of Rajasthan and the 'Pink City', was founded by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II in the 18th century. The Kalki Mandir stands inside the walled city at Sireh Deori Bazar / Tulsi Marg, Badi Chaupar, near Hawa Mahal and the City Palace area.

travel.airport: Jaipur International Airport, about 11-13 km away (verify).
travel.railway: Jaipur Junction railway station, about 3-4 km away (verify).
travel.road: In the walled city (Pink City) at Sireh Deori Bazar / Tulsi Marg, Badi Chaupar; reached by taxi, auto-rickshaw or on foot within the old city (note: vehicles may be restricted in the bazaar lanes).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Reported as approximately 6:00 AM-11:00 AM and 6:00 PM-8:00 PM daily (one video source says 5:30 AM-8:00 PM) - verify before visiting. Entry is free.
